newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Q2 private consumption up 2.9 pct vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Q2 private consumption up 2.9 pct vs yr ago.

text.p: Private consumption in Mexico rose by 2.9 percent in the second quarter compared to the second quarter of 1995, the government statistics institute INEGI said Friday.
Total supply of available goods and services -- consisting of GDP plus imports of goods and services -- rose 10.5 percent in the same period, INEGI said in a statement.
Mexican public investment rose 34.8 percent in the second quarter from the previous year while private investment rose 13.9 percent, it added.
INEGI said total supply rose to 1.596 trillion constant 1993 pesos in the second quarter from 1.444 trillion in the second quarter of 1995.
The result consisted of an increase of 7.2 percent in Gross Domestic Product and a real increase of 27.0 percent in imports, it added.
GDP made up 80.7 percent of total supply while the remaining 19.3 percent came from imports of goods and services.
INEGI sais all four components of total demand also rose, as follows:

Private consumption of goods and services rose 2.9 percent in real terms; government consumption rose 0.8 percent; gross formation of fixed capital grew 17.6 percent in real terms; and total exports of goods and services rose 14.5 percent in constant prices.
INEGI said that under the heading of gross fixed capital formation in the second quarter, public investment rose 34.8 percent and private investment rose 13.9 percent from a year earlier.
Public investment made up 20.4 percent of the total and private investment accounted for 79.6 percent.
Exports of goods rose by 18.7 percent in real terms, with manufacturing exports up 20.1 percent and crude and natural gas up 22.8 percent; while exports of services grew 10.7 percent.

INEGI said that in the second quarter of this year, private consumption made up 55.0 percent of total demand; exports of goods and services 21.7 percent; gross fixed capital formation 14.4 percent and government consumption 8.9 percent.

In the first half of 1996, INEGI said total supply of goods and services rose by 5.9 percent in real terms compared to the first six months of 1995. It said GDP grew 3.0 percent and imports of goods and services grew 20.5 percent.

With regard to total demand in the first half of 1996, it said that private consumption grew by 2.1 percent in real terms from a year before; government consumption grew 0.9 percent; gross fixed capital formation grew 5.9 percent; and exports of goods and services grew 14.0 percent.
